concerns.text: FR-008/SC-006 require validation against the INDEPENDENT published therapy-response signature (PMID 32012345). The plan instead derives the signature from GSE138852 responder labels ('therapy-response signature derived from GSE138852 responder vs. non-responder labels'). This changes the validation construct: a label-derived signature from a study dataset is not the independent published gene set, and GSE138852 is also the validation dataset — creating partial circularity the spec's assumption ('derived from a separate cohort and thus provides an unbiased validation set') explicitly guards against. The plan never mentions PMID 32012345 or how the published gene set will be obtained.

scVelo requires spliced/unspliced count layers (loom files), but the plan's data acquisition (Phase 1) downloads generic GEO supplementary files and preprocessing (Phase 2) builds a standard count matrix via Seurat. The plan never states how spliced/unspliced layers will be obtained for these four accessions. If the supplementary files are count matrices only, velocity is impossible regardless of the T004 retry logic — 'layer detection with explicit errors' reports the gap but the plan has no acquisition strategy (e.g., loom files, alevin/velocyto re-processing) to actually satisfy FR-003. This is a feasibility/methodology gap, not just an error-handling path.

concerns.location: plan.md: Phase Order table — Phase 6 (power analysis) after Phase 5 (fork-point detection)
concerns.text: FR-011's power analysis is placed AFTER fork-point detection. Power should be assessed on realized cell counts before or at the start of inference so that underpowered analyses are aborted before results are generated and interpreted. Reorder Phase 6 ahead of Phase 5, or state explicitly that Phase 5 outputs are discarded if power is insufficient.

The cross-dataset Spearman correlation is computed on 'top 3 fork-point genes' (spec target ≥0.80). A rank correlation over 3 items has very few possible values and near-zero resolution; the plan should state how ties/pairs across datasets are formed (e.g., correlation over the full ranked gene list with top-3 reported separately) so the ≥0.80 criterion is statistically interpretable rather than trivially unstable.
